primary_claim: Recent frontier LLMs (e.g. Opus 4.5) can leverage filler tokens or repeated problem statements to significantly improve no-CoT math performance, unlike pre-2024 models which cannot use filler tokens this way

effect.value: Opus 4.5: 45% to 51% (p=4e-7) with filler tokens; similar boost from repeats

contradicts_or_qualifies: Prior results showing LLMs released before 2024 can't leverage filler tokens to improve performance
stated_future_work: Investigate whether filler tokens/repeats help in other single-token-answer domains, e.g. code correctness/backdoor classification, as a proxy for steganography ability
Apply interpretability tools to filler tokens or repeats to understand why this helps
Study performance over time on other tasks requiring weak no-CoT meta-cognitive abilities
Discuss general results on no-CoT (single forward pass) time horizon for LLMs in a future post
limitations_stated: Datasets used are relatively arithmetic-heavy so results don't clearly distinguish arithmetic-specific help from general help
Easy-Comp-Math dataset may be contaminated or have label errors (accuracy <98% due to parsing issues)
Relative performance improvement comparisons across models may not be meaningful due to different problem subsets and difficulty distributions
Many smaller uplift values for weaker models aren't statistically significant and could be noise
Dataset intentionally not made public to reduce contamination risk
quote: Giving Opus 4.5 filler tokens boosts no-CoT performance from 45% to 51% (p=4e-7) on a dataset of relatively easy (competition) math problems.
